title: Cantonese Black Pepper Steak Sauce
description: A brief toast wakes up black pepper, which perfumes a smooth mushroom and beef pan sauce without overwhelming it.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: low-sodium beef broth
ingredients.note: Use plain unsalted beef broth at about 60 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: unsalted dry drinking sherry
ingredients.note: Use drinking sherry, without added salt.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

steps.title: Sweat the mushrooms
steps.text: Soften {bb} in {oil} over medium-low heat for 4 minutes until a little mushroom juice gathers in the skillet.

steps.title: Wake the pepper
steps.text: Stir in {pep} and {ga} for 20 seconds, then loosen the pan with {sh}.

steps.title: Make the pepper gravy
steps.text: Add {be}, {a} and {bs}. Simmer for 4 minutes, then take off heat, blend smooth and return to a simmer.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over thin steak slices. Pass the pepper mill separately for anyone who wants a sharper bite.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, use only 1/8 teaspoon black pepper and replace the sherry with water. Nutrition counts the full sherry before simmering. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 41 kcal, 1.2 g protein, 5.4 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 105 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 37 kcal, 1.2 g protein, 4.4 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 37 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
